steps.name: Gu Quan
steps.text: One tangerine cake... to go, please.

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: Oh, you're here.

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: Sending it to Victoria this time as well?

steps.name: Gu Quan
steps.text: No... Not sending it. I need to go back right away... Though it's hard to say if I even can go back.

steps.name: Gu Quan
steps.text: This time—

steps.name: Gu Quan
steps.text: *cough* *cough* *cough*! Just a snack for the road.

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: Wow, your cough's gotten pretty bad.

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: I don't think you should be eating sweets right now. I'll boil you up a bowl of loquat soup.

steps.name: Gu Quan
steps.text: I'm fine, I'm fine... It's not to do with my lungs.

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: Doesn't matter where the problem is, you've got to take care of yourself. You seen a doctor about it?

steps.name: Gu Quan
steps.text: Yes, yes. I don't have much time left, apparently.

steps.name: Gu Quan
steps.text: I'd say I'm beyond having to mind what I eat.

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: ...Huh?

steps.name: Gu Quan
steps.text: It's fine. Everyone has to die someday.

steps.name: Gu Quan
steps.text: I've done pretty much everything I needed to get done—

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: How can you say something like that?!

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: Didn't you... Didn't you say you still have family in Victoria? They're waiting for you to go home.

steps.name: Gu Quan
steps.text: Yes... I held onto hope that I could see them again, but it seems

steps.name: Gu Quan
steps.text: *cough*... that won't be happening...

steps.name: Gu Quan
steps.text: I might've been a useless good-for-nothing my entire life, but at least I can say I haven't disgraced what little ideals and righteousness I still have in me.

steps.name: Gu Quan
steps.text: But only now that I'm at the end have I realized I owe them far, far too much...

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: *sigh* Isn't that just how people are? Things like that happen from time to time. If you try and be the perfect people pleaser, you're a fool.

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: But surely you still want to go home, right?

steps.name: Gu Quan
steps.text: I want to see them, but if I don't, they'll have easier lives.

steps.name: Gu Quan
steps.text: That's just how people are... If you want to get something done, you need to put something down.

steps.name: Gu Quan
steps.text: Everyone else has put their things down, so I should too...

steps.name: Gu Quan
steps.text: I have been in your care for so many years now, Young Chef. Even my final few words in this reverie of mine are for your ears only.

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: Then...

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: Is there still... something you want?

steps.name: Gu Quan
steps.text: I want...

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: You need to pay more attention. Look at this spot you swept, it's still covered in ash.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: Make sure not to miss any corners either. Anything dirty has to be cleaned. We are moving out soon, and we cannot leave behind any trouble for the house's next owner.

steps.name: Ning's Butler
steps.text: It is rather late, Mr. Ning. Where are you headed off to?

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: Oh, don't mind me, just going out for a walk.

steps.name: Ning's Servant
steps.text: Mr. Ning's been acting really odd today.

steps.name: Ning's Servant
steps.text: Why's he spending his Mid-Autumn Festival watching us clean the house instead of gazing at the moon?

steps.name: Ning's Butler
steps.text: That's enough questions out of you. Focus on your sweeping.

steps.name: Ning's Butler
steps.text: With such brilliant moonlight tonight, we should give it a pristine spot to land on.

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: How did I... get here...

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: Grandfather's study?
Her mind lurches on the edge of consciousness. She feels as though she has forgotten something important.
An old book lies upon the desk in silence.

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: Annals of Yan, Volume 124, Supplement 17... 1062... Since when was there such a book in the Imperial Historical Records?

spans.text: ... 1062... Since when was there such a book in the Imperial Historical Records?

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: ...Grandfather?

steps.name: Prison Guard A
steps.text: It's been years since there was a criminal thrown into the fifth floor of this prison. What's the story tonight?

steps.name: Prison Guard B
steps.text: Assassinating someone at court. The Imperial Guard themselves are dragging the culprit here.

steps.name: Prison Guard A
steps.text: What a ruthless—!

steps.name: Prison Guard B
steps.text: Shh!

steps.name: Prison Guard B
steps.text: Don't think too hard about it, and don't ask too many questions. Just keep a close eye on the culprit. You and I won't be enough to fix any mistakes.
It seems that everything I've run into since my return to Baizao has been part of some grand plan.
A trail of clues laid out in front of me like bait, leading towards a dead end.

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: Not only was the perpetrator highly skilled in kung fu, but they also had intimate knowledge of the Judicial Review Office's layout. They must have been working with Yu Cheng for quite some time.

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: Yu Cheng asked you to take notes during his trial. This is why you stand here now, and it is also the reason I cannot allow you to participate any further.

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: Whatever Yu Cheng's plan, you are most certainly a part of it.

steps.name: Masked Individual
steps.text: Deputy Minister Lin, surely you wouldn't ask if you didn't know the answer already?

steps.name: Masked Individual
steps.text: Can you not see the truth, or do you simply pretend you can't because you don't dare to?

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: What makes you so dead-set on the case, Censor Jie Zhen?
As the moons slowly sink into the west, their light passes through the barred window and scatters on the far wall of the cell. The night air condenses into dew, beading on Lin Qingyan's brow.
Were it not for the scent of mold, this prison would actually be a good place to meditate.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Indeed. While I was waiting here, I managed to figure out many things that have been on my mind.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: It was you who set the scrollery on fire.
Was it an answer I gave you here, or one you puzzled out beforehand?

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: We meet again, Deputy Minister Lin.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Hey, I'm not in the mood to discuss snacks with you right now. I've got people to save!

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: Calm down, take it easy. Is it any use being so high-strung when you have so much to do?

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: What do you know—

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: All I know is that if the heat ain't right, don't take off the lid.

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: *sigh* You can't skip out on meals if you have something big to do. If you don't eat, you're not getting anything done.

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: Here, try this. Is this the tangerine cake you're looking for?

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: You... Weren't you always saying I wouldn't be able to find it, even if I searched all of Baizao?

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: I also said I'm the best chef in all of Baizao. As long as the taste exists, I can replicate it.

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: And this one's my own creation. It won't count for our bet.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Isn't this the same tangerine cake you made before—
Despite her skepticism, Blaze shoves a cake into her mouth.
She has tried many fine dishes over the last few days, and learned a lot about how to critique food during that time. The cake in front of her cannot be considered 'tasty'.
Xingzhu was right. Too much sugar will overwhelm the fragrance of the tangerine peel, while too much oil destroys the texture of the cake itself.
It is not a tasty snack...
But it is an exact match for the taste in her memories.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: How do you...

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: How do you know this recipe?

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: You were so hung up on my tangerine cake not being sweet enough. It got me wondering what kind of chef would make them that sweet.

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: Then I thought, what if the one who made them so sweet didn't do it for the taste?

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: That means...

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: You said you ate these in Victoria, right?

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: I'm reminded of a regular customer I had many years ago. He always ordered some tangerine cakes, and said he was going to send some off to his daughter in a foreign land.

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: I told him they'd spoil long before they got to her.

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: But he refused to believe me. He'd process it a bit himself, and wrap it up in layer after layer of letter paper. You could barely tell if it was a letter or some food by the end of it.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: You knew him!

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: He came here... I've been searching for him all this time...

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Do you... know what happened to him...?

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: I wouldn't say I knew him. He was just a regular customer of many years.

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: I vaguely remember him always coming over before it was even bright out to order the cheapest breakfast I had on the menu, then he'd sit by the window, like he was waiting for someone.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Waiting for someone? Who...?

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: How should I know? See for yourself.
Day breaks.
The faint full moons brush against the horizon. As the night come to a close, there are perhaps many in slumber, enjoying dreams of happy reunions.
Diligent hawkers are up early setting up their stalls, their shouts echoing down the streets, rousing the sleepers of the metropolis.
Blaze spots a familiar figure by the street corner.
This small restaurant and that serene manor are separated by no more than a street corner. A fact barely worth noticing during normal times.
Was this what he was looking at, year after year?

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: It's you...

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: It's really you...

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: You're here.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: I never thought I would see you again in my lifetime.
The man leaning against the corner is clothed in near-rags. He grasps a mooncake in his hands, his face awash in crumbs, ignorant of his guest.
A smear of light leaks in through the bars of his cell window, painting the criminal's gaunt face in stark relief.

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: The Judicial Review Office is truly kind. Even us prisoners get a mooncake for the Mid-Autumn Festival.

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: It's delicious. Want a bite?

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: No need. I will be having my meals in this prison soon enough. I will have my own to enjoy.

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: Pity, we still have so much to talk about. It's not quite the same without something to munch on, right?
The old man lets out a dry laugh, taking a seat across from the shabbily-dressed prisoner.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: For decades, you have wanted to ask an old man like me your questions. I suppose today is your lucky day?

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: You should hate me, Mr. Ning.

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: You were one step away from being able to go back home without a heavy heart, one step away from enjoying your twilight years with your family.

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: Just one small step... Hahahahaha.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: I really should hate you, when you put it like that. I would like nothing more than to charge at you and tear at your flesh with my teeth.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: But on second thought, you have given up decades of your life and your position as Deputy Minister at the Judicial Review Office for me, spending the rest of your years within this cell.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: No matter how you look at it, it should be you who hates me.

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: Hahahaha... You're overthinking it, Mr. Ning.

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: I said it before, but I was never any good at my job, or at being a decent human being... Not like Gu Quan.

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: I'm a glutton, you see, the type that loves sniffing out deep, hidden truths. I tore open shells to get at the flesh, and got addicted to the sweet, sweet taste of marrow. I'll do anything for it, even if it leaves my hands bloodied and my teeth shattered.

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: During all these years, you were the biggest, plumpest shellbeast on my dining table. How could I ever hate you?

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: Even if I were to hate... It wouldn't be for anything on my side.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: Your teeth are still in fine shape. I never saw them chip while they were gnawing on my old bones.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: But Yu Cheng, why were you so sure I would have come to see you today?

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: If I had just walked away from all this, all your plots and plans would have gone to waste, no?

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: Hahahaha... Because I understand you. I understand you far too well, Mr. Ning.

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: I simply had to gamble, that during the years you spent bobbing around the hierarchy of mandarins, you would dirty your hands, but still retain your humanity.

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: You let Gu Quan live on while he was right under your nose, after all, and raised his daughter to boot.

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: You care about the fate of that child... Those two children, rather. You wanted to see those girls live carefree, innocent lives while you yet live...

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: You knew that if you did not relent one day, they would never know peace.

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: And so you came to see me... You had to.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: You have looked into these matters already... It seems you managed to find out most of what should have been found out.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: How long did it take you?

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: I only finished deciphering the clues and piecing them all together last year. It shames me to admit as a deputy minister, but my pace was a bit too slow.

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: Gu Quan, on the other hand? He managed to figure it all out years ago.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: I never considered that...

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: The year he returned to Baizao, you managed to put him under your watch. But you never thought he would copy decades worth of letters from your home.

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: By peering through all those letters between grand mandarins and nobles, he, a ninth-rank ceremonial officer, found every survivor of that murder case. He unraveled the threads and pieced the truth together.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: Gu Quan's diligence knew no bounds. I underestimated him.

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: Anything more you wish to say, Mr. Ning?

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: Hahahaha... What is there left to say? What sins must be admitted, I shall admit.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: I really did send someone to kill the Minister of Justice who presided over the Grand Preceptor's case.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: But not because he accused me of being the Grand Preceptor's collaborator in treason...

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: Rather, because the Grand Preceptor's treason was a miscarriage of justice all along.

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: Indulge me in my curiosity, Deputy Minister Lin. When did you figure it out?

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: I suspected it was you who set Ding Feng Lou alight.

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: Why? What would I have to do with that incident?

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Call it a hunch.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Though you might not have used your kung fu at the time, a mask was not enough to prevent me from thinking that person's figure and skills were familiar. Very familiar.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Afterwards, at the Judicial Review Office, you sought me out and managed to cement this particular suspicion in my mind.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Come to think of it, you must have been in close contact with Yu Cheng as early as when I was preparing to impeach him. I never considered the possibility you were already cooperating with him at the time.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: From the scrollery fire to the hanging scroll in the Ning Manor, and then on to the fire at Ding Feng Lou. This recent string of mysteries was you trying to lead me along a trail of clues, wasn't it?

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: That was rather rushed and sloppy, now that I look back.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: And the fire at the Feast of a Hundred Delicacies...?

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: I must regret to inform you that was not my doing, truly. Merely an unexpected turn that happened to align with our goal.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Why did you two do all this?

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: Ridiculous as it may sound, this all started with an old case. Not a large one, yet not small either.

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: A case I happened upon by chance after I joined the Department of Discipline and Supervision.

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: The Minister of Justice, assassinated by a beggar in the middle of the street. A case I could barely believe, yet one hastily closed without meaningful buildup or a satisfying conclusion.

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: Though the assassin had been executed, his identity, his motive... There were simply too many vague unknowns in the file.

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: As I dug deeper, I noticed that every thread led towards an even bigger case, a case that had snipped all those threads short.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: The Grand Preceptor's treason...

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: You've investigated that case too.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: The betrayal of the three Grand Ministers, a case large enough to shake the court, and one that implicates countless others. Forget finding the truth, even just mentioning the Grand Preceptor's name at the time was the greatest of taboos.

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: 'The Grand Preceptor incited the prince to regicide.' This was all the history books had to say on the matter.

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: But nobody knows the truth of what happened the night the old True Lung passed away.

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: Who was it who mobilized the city guard? Who went into the palace?

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: Only later did I realize I was not the only one looking into this case.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Was this how you got to know Yu Cheng?

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: Should I rather call it fowlbeasts of a feather, or friendship at first sight?

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: You said the two of you weren't able to follow the trail, so how did you determine the Grand Preceptor was wrongly accused?

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: It wasn't our research that lead to this conclusion.

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: The one who brought everything to light was Gu Quan.

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: Why?

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: Do you seriously not know why?

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: Of course I do. I just wanted to ask you how this 'why' tasted when you said it aloud.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: ...The people cry out, their hearts uneasy...

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: Only those who have experienced the struggle know that Yan's current peace and prosperity were hard-won.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: It was a very, very long time ago.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: The old True Lung was diligent. At the time, Originium industries were beginning to change the structure of this great land. Even during Yan's turbulent times, he did not allow her to fall behind the other nations of Terra.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: And so it was that a great hero was infected with Oripathy in his twilight years. Believing his days were numbered, his many policies began to stray into bias and imbalance.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: At the time, the prince wished to stop the True Lung... and the Grand Preceptor stood by his side.

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: This supposed support was her urging the prince to seize the throne?

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: The old True Lung died the night the prince entered the palace to admonish him. As for the prince? His whereabouts since that night are unknown. Such a tumultuous event demanded an explanation.

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: ...Which required someone to be charged with everything.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: Do you think the current True Lung was unaware of all this...?

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: Hmph.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: Changes in the court naturally lead to unrest among the masses. 'The Purge of Traitors'. A very fitting slogan.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: The then-young True Lung acted with an iron fist to sweep away many courtiers with evil intent, stabilizing the situation as quickly as possible. This ensured this spell of court intrigue never made it outside the walls of the Forbidden City.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: For forty years, I assumed I was the only one aside from the True Lung himself to still remember what transpired.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: Until ten or so years after that case ended, that young man stood in front of me once again.

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: I fear you speak of that time too lightly, Mr. Ning.

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: It was not only traitors who were 'swept away'. There was also the entirety of the Grand Preceptor's family, twenty-eight in all.

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: They were all sent to prison. Some committed suicide in their cells to prove their innocence. Those who lived were exiled. I tried to find some trace of them, but it was no use. Couldn't find a single one.

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: Except for a child... Spirited away during the turmoil, still swaddled in a blanket.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: I never considered the possibility she still lived, yet never truly believed she had died.

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: It seems you've met her.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: A few days ago. Her appearance is... not too similar. But their personality? It's like two peas in a pod.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: Gu Quan never spoke a word about that child's whereabouts during the decade he spent in Baizao, right up until his death...

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: I'm sure you're now well aware of why he died on the road back to Victoria.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: Yu Cheng, you old bastard.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: You used Gu Quan's own death to ensure there was no possibility of anyone finding that child, which also gave you an opportunity to investigate me.

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: At the time I assumed Gu Quan had no success in his exhaustive research into the Grand Preceptor case, which prompted him to leave Baizao in despair.

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: It was only after many years that I realized it was not the so-called truth that he sought. He had long since found the answers to those troubles you mentioned earlier.

steps.name: Yu Cheng
steps.text: What he hoped I would do was something else entirely.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: I don't understand...

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Are you telling me you two knew all along that Blaze was the orphan from that case?

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: Your investigation should have already revealed that Gu Quan and Yu Cheng knew each other.

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: After taking the child away, Gu Quan kept the secret of her whereabouts to himself for decades. But before he met his untimely end, he confided in the only 'friend' he had, Yu Cheng.

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: After his death, Yu Cheng immediately began to search for her.

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: However, he was unable to personally act as deputy minister at the Judicial Review Office. He entrusted the task of performing discreet inquiries to me, far from the center of court politics, so as to not attract attention.

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: By the time I found her in Victoria, she was already infected.

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: I could not take her back to Baizao right away. For the sake of protecting her, I had no choice but to place her in the care of a medical organization that treated the Infected.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: So it was you...

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: You were already aligned at the time, I see.

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: But you were also part of this plan from early on, Deputy Minister Lin.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: What do you mean?

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: How was it you were able to find Blaze's trail? How were you able to come across those files pertaining to her past? Surely you didn't just attribute them to chance?

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: Yu Cheng would not have told you these himself. The risk was too great. There could not be a third person who knew of this in all of Terra.

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: But he was always searching for a suitable candidate... One with courage, who stood for truth.

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: He has long since been ready to give his life for this cause. I am happy to dirty my hands doing what must be done in his stead.

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: But it's not enough. We needed someone pure and innocent, one who could use honest means to lay bare the truth.

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: It's nearly time.

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: We still have one last opportunity.

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: Do you still wish to bring the truth out into the light of day, Deputy Minister Lin?
